sentences: Out of drifting mist, a great mountain rises and seems to twist as it climbs.
Water trickles down between the rocks, and tall pines stretch out their branches.
This is the moment when winter is just letting go and the mountain is waking up.
This is Early Spring, by Guo Xi, a painter of China's Northern Song dynasty.
It is a hanging scroll in ink and light colour on silk, just over one and a half metres tall, and it belongs to the National Palace Museum in Taipei.
Along the left side, in small characters, is the painter's own signature: Early Spring, painted by Guo Xi in the renzi year.
That year corresponds to 1072.
A date written by the artist himself is rare for a painting this old, and precious for historians.
Guo Xi worked at the court of Emperor Shenzong.
In those years, new government offices and palace halls were decorated with his landscapes, and the museum suggests that this painting may once have been made for just such a building.
Now look down the centre of the scroll.
From the boulders and tall pines in front, past the writhing middle slopes, up through the mist to the highest peak, the forms join into one continuous movement.
The whole mountain seems alive.
Look closely at the rock surfaces.
Curling strokes are layered one over another until the rocks look like heaped clouds, a manner known as cloud-scroll texture.
Dark and pale ink mingle, so that mist seems to wrap around the stone.
Now look at the trees.
The tips of the branches bend and split like the claws of a crab.
These trees have only just come through the winter, and they are on the point of putting out new leaves.
Then search for the people.
There are boats by the water, and on the mountain paths travellers and people gathering firewood.
High in the valley stand large halls.
This is a mountain you can not only look at, but walk through and live in.
Guo Xi's ideas on painting survive in a text called The Lofty Message of Forests and Streams.
It describes three kinds of distance: looking up at height, looking back into depth, and looking out across level space.
Early Spring gathers all three into a single picture.
In the upper right is a poem added in 1759 by the Qianlong Emperor of the Qing dynasty.
Together with Fan Kuan's Travelers Among Mountains and Streams in the same museum, it is counted as a great milestone of Northern Song landscape painting.
Step back and see it whole.
All over the cold mountain, mist is rising like steam from the earth.
Today, look around you for one small sign of something waking up, a first hint of spring in your own surroundings.
